value.rationale: PASS: Monicity in all dyadic index blocks is a naturally defined structural property of Stern polynomials and the simple exact Tribonacci law yields a genuine quantitative consequence for the published reciprocal-index counting problem: density zero. The bound is intermediate and not conjecturally optimal; it is not advertised as a solution of Gawron polylogarithmic conjecture. A finite-state exact infinite enumeration and power saving are mathematically useful regardless of absent downstream theorem.

final_claim: For Stern polynomials the exact binary-block generating functions for monic B_n and odd-index monic B_n are z(1+z)/(1-z-z^2-z^3) and z(1-z^2)/(1-z-z^2-z^3). Hence both block counts satisfy a Tribonacci recurrence. Since reciprocal indices are odd and monic, the number of reciprocal indices <=X is O(X^theta), theta=log_2(lambda)<1, lambda the real Tribonacci growth root; thus reciprocal indices have density zero.
limitations: Positive index only; monic superset; theta between zero and one, no polylog upper claim.
